extracted.intended_audience: corporate leaders, executives, and organizational decision-makers (especially those handling crisis/public communications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for when corporate or organizational leaders should apologize publicly and how to craft an effective public apology; covers decision conditions, risks, and the essential components of a successful apology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity in public apologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the stakes are so high, leaders should not extend public apologies often or lightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies are risky and political; be selective. Consider alternatives and avoid reflexive or cosmetic apologies that may do more harm than good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apology should serve an important purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The apology is likely to serve an important purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only apologize when the act of apologizing will achieve a meaningful objective (e.g., restore trust, prevent escalation, enable remediation). The author recommends that one or more specific conditions should apply before apologizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offense must be of serious consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The offense is of serious consequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer apologizing when the wrongdoing has significant negative impact; trivial or ambiguous matters may not warrant a public apology and could undermine credibility if overused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of leader assuming responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: It's appropriate that the leader assume responsibility for the offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should apologize only when it fits the locus of responsibility; taking on responsibility unnecessarily can be risky, but failing to assume responsibility when appropriate can worsen harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leader is the only one who can get the job done
rubrics_metrics.description: The leader is the only one who can get the job done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If remediation, reconciliation, or corrective action requires the leader’s unique authority or involvement, that increases the case for a public apology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of speaking lower than cost of staying silent
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of saying something is likely lower than the cost of staying silent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh reputational, legal, political, and operational costs. Apologize when silence would produce greater harm than the risks associated with apologizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public apology is politically risky; every word matters
rubrics_metrics.description: A public apology is a risky move. It's highly political, and every word matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft language carefully; anticipate political and media framing. Understand that refusal to apologize can be read as strength or recklessness, and that readiness to apologize can be seen as character or weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for transformation if apology succeeds
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful apology can turn enmity into personal and organizational triumph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the upside: a well-timed, sincere apology can repair relationships and reputations. Factor potential reconciliation and long-term benefits into the decision calculus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid apologies that are 'too little, too late, or transparently tactical'
rubrics_metrics.description: An apology that's too little, too late, or too transparently tactical can open the floodgates to individual and institutional ruin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the apology is substantive, timely, and perceived as authentic. Avoid gestures that appear merely tactical or manipulative, as they can exacerbate backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of the mistake or wrongdoing
rubrics_metrics.description: A good apology includes acknowledgment of the mistake or wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state what went wrong so stakeholders understand you recognize the specific harm; vague or evasive language undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A good apology includes acceptance of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should explicitly accept responsibility (as appropriate) rather than deflecting blame; this demonstrates accountability and fosters trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of regret
rubrics_metrics.description: A good apology includes expression of regret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey sincere remorse; tone and wording should communicate genuine contrition rather than formulaic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance the offense will not be repeated
rubrics_metrics.description: A good apology includes assurance that the offense will not be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to concrete corrective actions or systemic changes and, where possible, outline steps that will prevent recurrence to restore confidence.
